settings.name_in_paper: Batched Lipschitz bandits with limited memory (W bits, at most B batches, adaptive batch boundaries allowed)
unmapped: Learner's reward-dependent mutable state is limited to W_mem bits after every observation (public seed, round/batch indices and current batch's action sequence are free)
Batch boundaries may be chosen adaptively at the start of each batch
Learner knows the memory budget W_mem
Action space [0,1]^d with sup norm; mean reward 1-Lipschitz with values in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: Let $\X=[0,1]^d$ with the sup norm, and let $\Lip_1(\X)$ denote the class of one-Lipschitz functions from $\X$ to $[0,1]$. ... The complete reward-dependent mutable state satisfies $M_t\in\{0,1\}^W$ ... A policy partitions the $T$ rounds into at most $B$ nonempty batches ... Each batch boundary is chosen adaptively at the start of that batch.

settings.name_in_paper: Lipschitz bandits with one bit of memory and batch boundaries fixed in advance (lower bound)
unmapped: Learner's reward-dependent mutable state is one bit
Batch boundaries fixed in advance (depend only on the public seed)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathfrak R_T^{\mathrm{fix}}(B,W)$ denote minimax regret over policies with batch boundaries fixed in advance.

settings.name_in_paper: Lipschitz bandits with one bit of memory and adaptive batch boundaries
unmapped: Learner's reward-dependent mutable state is one bit
Batch boundaries chosen adaptively at batch starts (timing indices are free and can retain information)
settings.definition_quote: We now consider $W=1$, the smallest nonzero memory budget, to determine the attainable regret and whether fixed boundaries remain sufficient.

algorithms.name: Policy processing groups at fixed scales (active-set construction in groups + refinement)
Combined fixed-boundary policy (fixed action for B=1, full-domain refinement for B=2, hierarchy for 3<=B<B_0, groups for B>=B_0)
Two-batch full-domain refinement (fine grid exploration then exploitation)
One-bit adaptive-boundary comparison policy (timing-encoded incumbent comparisons)

source.label: thm:joint-frontier
source.quote: There exist constants $c_d,C_d,T_d>0$, depending only on $d$, such that, for every $T\ge T_d$ and all $B,W$, \mathfrak R_T(B,W) \ge c_d\left[ T^{\frac{d+1}{d+2}} \vee\frac{T^{\beta_{d,B}}}{B^2} \vee T^{\frac{d+2}{d+3}} \bigl(1+(B-1)W\bigr)^{-\frac1{d(d+3)}} \right].

results.notes: Minimax lower bound over 1-Lipschitz means with [0,1] rewards; hard instances are Bernoulli. B = M_batch. beta_{d,B}=(d+1)/((d+2)(1-(d+2)^{-B})) written explicitly.

bound.regime: T >= T_d and W >= C_d log(eT)

tuning: fixed batch boundaries; construction chosen by B (fixed action B=1, full-domain refinement B=2, hierarchy 3<=B<B_0, groups B>=B_0)

source.label: thm:joint-frontier
source.quote: If $W\ge C_d\log(eT)$, then \mathfrak R_T(B,W) \le C_d\log(eT)\left[ T^{\frac{d+1}{d+2}} \vee\frac{T^{\beta_{d,B}}}{B^2} \vee T^{\frac{d+2}{d+3}} \bigl(1+(B-1)W\bigr)^{-\frac1{d(d+3)}} \right]. ... the upper bound is attained with fixed batch boundaries.

results.notes: Attained with fixed batch boundaries, so it also holds in the adaptive-boundary class.

bound.regime: T sufficiently large, W >= C_d log(eT)

source.label: cor:batch-complexity
source.quote: For a dimension-dependent constant $\varrho_d>0$, all sufficiently large $T$, and $W\gtrsim_d\log(eT)$, \mathcal B_T(W;\varrho_d) =\widetilde\Theta_d\!\left( \log\log T\vee\frac{T^{d/(d+2)}}{W} \right).

results.notes: Quantity is batch complexity: minimal number of batches B such that minimax regret <= rho_d log(eT) T^{(d+1)/(d+2)}. Explicit form from Appendix eq (appendix-batch-complexity-bounds).

bound.regime: T sufficiently large, W >= C_d log(eT)

source.label: cor:batch-complexity
source.quote: For a dimension-dependent constant $\varrho_d>0$, all sufficiently large $T$, and $W\gtrsim_d\log(eT)$, \mathcal B_T(W;\varrho_d) =\widetilde\Theta_d\!\left( \log\log T\vee\frac{T^{d/(d+2)}}{W} \right).

results.notes: Lower bound on number of batches needed for near-optimal regret; explicit log factors from the appendix proof.

source.label: lem:routing-memory
source.quote: There exist dimension-dependent constants $c_d,C_d>0$ such that, for the scales above with $Tr^2\ge C_d$, if (B-1)W\le c_ds^{-d}, then \mathfrak R_T(B,W) \ge c_d\min\{Tr,sr^{-d-2}\}. The bound allows batch boundaries chosen adaptively at batch starts.

results.notes: Intermediate scale-parametrized lower bound; optimized yields joint term of Theorem 3.1.

source.label: lem:two-scale-upper

results.notes: Scales s, r are algorithm tuning; resource conditions recorded as conditions.

tuning: fixed batch boundaries, L+2 <= B batches

source.label: lem:in-memory-branch
source.quote: For some $C_d>0$ and all sufficiently large $T$, if W\ge C_d(s^{-d}+b_{B,r}), C_dLb_{B,r}r^{-d-2}\le T/2, then a policy ... with fixed batch boundaries and at most $L+2\le B$ batches satisfies ... \le C_d\left[Lb_{B,r}s^{-\gamma_d(L)}+b_{B,r}sr^{-d-2}+Tr\right].

conditions: holds with unrestricted memory and for every W >= 0

source.label: lem:batch-depth-transfer
source.quote: Fix $d\ge1$. There are constants $c_d,T_d>0$ such that, for $T\ge T_d$ and $2\le B\le T$, \mathfrak R_T^{\mathrm{bat}}(B) \ge c_d\frac{T^{\beta_{d,B}}}{B^2}. The same bound holds for $\mathfrak R_T(B,W)$ for every integer $W\ge0$.

results.notes: Transfer of Feng et al. (2022) Theorem 8 from Gaussian to Bernoulli rewards and at-most-B batches.

bound.regime: B = 2, T sufficiently large, any W >= 0

tuning: fine grid resolution r = smallest dyadic radius >= max{(A log(4T)/T)^{1/(d+3)}, 2^{-xi_d W}}

source.label: eq:two-batch-upper-curve
source.quote: We first establish a bound valid for every integer $W\ge0$: for sufficiently large $T$, \mathfrak R_T(2,W) \le C_dT\min\left\{1, \max\left\{ \left(\frac{\log(4T)}{T}\right)^{1/(d+3)}, 2^{-c_dW} \right\}\right\}.

results.notes: Stated within the proof of the upper bound of Theorem 3.1, not as a numbered statement.

source.label: thm:one-bit-timing
source.quote: There exist constants $c_d,C_d>0$, depending only on $d$, such that, for every $T\ge2$ and all $B$, c_dTB^{-1/(d+2)} \le \mathfrak R_T(B,1) \le C_dT\left(\frac{\log(eB)}{B}\right)^{1/(d+2)}.

tuning: adaptive batch boundaries encoding comparison variables in timing

source.label: thm:one-bit-timing
source.quote: There exist constants $c_d,C_d>0$, depending only on $d$, such that, for every $T\ge2$ and all $B$, c_dTB^{-1/(d+2)} \le \mathfrak R_T(B,1) \le C_dT\left(\frac{\log(eB)}{B}\right)^{1/(d+2)}.

results.notes: Uses adaptive batch boundaries; mutable-state guarantee only (timing indices are free).

conditions: policies with batch boundaries fixed in advance
results.notes: Theta(T): upper side is trivial (Reg <= T). More generally, Appendix E gives R^fix(B,W) >= c_d T 2^{-W/d} for fixed boundaries; and Appendix A gives R_T(B,W) >= c_d T 2^{-(B-1)W/d} for any policy.

conditions: exploration rounds U_E <= C_d q_rho rho^{-d-2} must be <= T/2
number of exploration batches Q_E + 1 <= M_batch

source.label: lem:one-bit-fixed-accuracy
source.quote: For sufficiently large $A_d^{\mathrm{conf}}$, the construction below has exactly two mutable configurations ... If $U_E\le T/2$, appending exploitation gives a policy $\mathcal A$ satisfying ... \le C_d\bigl(q_\rho\rho^{-d-1}+T\rho\bigr). The policy belongs to $\mathfrak A_{B,1}$ whenever also $Q_E+1\le B$.

results.notes: Fixed-accuracy building block for the one-bit upper bound.
